candidates: When writing tests for MD integrators (thermostat or barostat classes), prefer convergence / truncation-error tests over pure reversibility (forward-then-backward) tests. Specifically, verify that n full steps of δ and 2n half-steps of δ/2 produce results whose difference shrinks as O(δ³) as δ decreases; this directly checks a physical promise of the integrator and is far more likely to catch subtle implementation bugs than a round-trip test alone.
Bug-fix MRs must include a changelog entry in `changelog.d/` created with `scriv`, describing what was broken and how it was fixed. Check that the changelog checklist item is ticked before approving.

When using `np.allclose` in numerical round-trip or reversibility tests for MD simulations, choose an `atol` generous enough to be machine-portable across platforms; tolerances as tight as 1e-6 have been observed to cause spurious CI failures due to floating-point variance. Prefer 1e-5 or verify empirically across platforms before committing to a stricter value.
